title: Idempotent data for the selected finite completion factor before transfer
statement: Let R be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], S a commutative R-algebra, q a prime of S, and S' an R-subalgebra finite as an R-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let g belong to S', with its image outside q, and suppose the canonical away-localization map S'_g to S_g is bijective [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Put p = q contracted to R, Rp = R_p, Sq = S_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], Ip and Iq their maximal ideals, and Rph and Sqh their completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let f:Rp to Sq be the local base map. Put T = Rph tensor_R S', U = Rph tensor_R S, let j:T to U be the tensor inclusion, and put gamma = 1 tensor g in T. Let psi:Rph to Sqh be a ring homomorphism satisfying, for all n, x and a, eval_n(x) = a mod Ip^n implies eval_n(psi(x)) = f(a) mod Iq^n. Let phi:U to Sqh be any ring homomorphism with phi(x tensor y) = psi(x) times the image of y in Sqh. There exist e,v in T such that e^2=e, v gamma=e, phi(j(e))=1, phi composed with j is surjective, and phi(j(t))=0 implies e t=0 for every t in T. This is only finite-tensor factor data; it asserts no splitting or equivalence for U.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime), finite product decomposition, invertibility of g on its selected factor, and the sanity check for the completed base map.

proof.text: Contract q to q' in S'. Apply Localization.awayMap_surjective_iff to clear powers of g from every element of S. Since g is outside q, these powers witness that S'.saturation along q.primeCompl intersected with S' is the whole ring. Localization.localRingHom_bijective_of_saturated_inf_eq_top gives bijectivity of the canonical localRingHom l from S' localized at q' to S localized at q. RingEquiv.ofBijective makes this a ring equivalence L. IsLocalRing.map_maximalIdeal_of_surjective identifies the image of the maximal ideal with Iq. At every power of the maximal ideal, Ideal.quotientEquiv gives a quotient equivalence. Apply RingTheory.pair_henselization_completion_data [lem-weil-pbc-henselization-completion-data] to obtain alpha and its coordinate formula; the private completion_equiv_of_ringEquiv helper handles transport along the equality of ideals.

The contracted ideal q' is prime and lies over p by the definitions of contraction and the subalgebra structure. Apply AdicCompletion.completion_finite_extension_decomposition R S' p and let q0 be the index q'. Prove the local-ring square by IsLocalization.ringHom_ext and Localization.localRingHom_to_map. For each x and n take a quotient representative a with Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective. Apply the quotient formulas for theta, alpha and psi, then the local-ring square; AdicCompletion.ext_eval_a (Lean: ext_evalₐ) gives alpha(theta(q0,x))=psi(x). The same coordinate calculation proves alpha's compatibility on S'. The S'-algebra property of the product equivalence and the factorization x tensor y=(x tensor 1)(1 tensor y) identify its value on tensors. TensorProduct.induction_on, additivity, and the given formula for phi show phi(j(t))=alpha(E(t)(q0)) for all t.

The image E(gamma)(q0) is a unit, since the image of g is a unit in the local ring at q' by IsLocalization.map_units and remains a unit under the completion map. Apply the proved private factor_idempotent helper to E.toRingEquiv, q0, alpha, phi.comp j and gamma. That helper pulls Pi.single q0 1 back to e and Pi.single q0 c back to v, where c is an inverse of E(gamma)(q0). Applying the injective E reduces idempotence and v*gamma=e to componentwise equations, with a case split on equality to q0. The projection formula gives phi(j(e))=1. Pulling back Pi.single q0 (alpha.symm b) proves surjectivity. If phi(j(t))=0, injectivity of alpha gives E(t)(q0)=0; every component of E(e*t) is zero, proving e*t=0. This handles arbitrary complementary factors, including no complementary factor.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_completion_factor_idempotent
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (q : PrimeSpectrum S)
    (S' : Subalgebra R S) [Module.Finite R S']
    (g : S') (hg : g.1 ∉ q.asIdeal)
    (haway : Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap S'.val.toRingHom g)) :
    let p : Ideal R := q.comap (algebraMap R S)
    let Rp := Localization.AtPrime p
    let Sq := Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal
    let Ip := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Rp
    let Iq := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Sq
    let Rph := AdicCompletion Ip Rp
    let Sqh := AdicCompletion Iq Sq
    let f : Rp →+* Sq := Localization.localRingHom p q.asIdeal (algebraMap R S) rfl
    let T := TensorProduct R Rph S'
    let U := TensorProduct R Rph S
    let j := (TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R Rph) S'.val).toRingHom
    let γ := TensorProduct.tmul R (1 : Rph) g
    ∀ (ψ : Rph →+* Sqh),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Rph) (a : Rp),
        AdicCompletion.evalₐ Ip n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ip ^ n) a →
        AdicCompletion.evalₐ Iq n (ψ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Iq ^ n) (f a)) →
      ∀ (φ : U →+* Sqh),
        (∀ (x : Rph) (y : S), φ (TensorProduct.tmul R x y) =
          ψ x * algebraMap Sq Sqh (algebraMap S Sq y)) →
        ∃ e v : T, IsIdempotentElem e ∧ v * γ = e ∧ φ (j e) = 1 ∧
          Function.Surjective (φ.comp j) ∧ (∀ t, φ (j t) = 0 → e * t = 0)
